chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abu al-Abbas who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sanctify Medina?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. He sanctified Bareed by planting therein.' I said, '(What about) its hunting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The people would not be belied.'

key_terms.بَرِيداً: A specific area or spot of land
key_terms.غَضَاها: Planted therein (referring to marking the boundary)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting in the sanctified area of Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the specific geographical boundaries of Medina's sanctity (*Haram*), defined by the *Bareed* (a distance marker) and physical demarcations like planted trees. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition extends to hunting within this zone, emphasizing that the boundaries are clear and recognizable to the public, preventing ambiguity in religious practice. This reflects the Shia scholarly view on the tangible and spiritual sanctity of the Prophet's city, linking it to broader concepts of sacred space in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from Abu Al Abbas who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Harram of Rasool-Allahsaww is Al-Medina?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes. Hesaww sanctified a spot if Bareyda (a certain area of land) by planting therein’. I said, ‘(What about) hunting in (such a sacred area)?’ Heasws said: ‘The people would not be belied’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban from abu al-‘Abbas who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’Is al-Madinah the sacred place of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause?’ He (the Imam) replied, ’Yes, he made it a one square Barid (a certain area of land) with its trees an area of sacred status.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ’What about hunting in such area?’ He (the Imam) replied, ’People’s words are not rejected.’” (Please consult Fatwa for this Hadith)
